1, SCOPE 1.1 This method covers the determination of benzene, toluene, C8 and
heavier aromatics, and total aromatics in the concentration range from I "O to 30 percent of the individual aromatic compounds listed above in the following products: (i) aviation gasolines (we 1S: 1604-1967*), (ii) reformer products having a final boiling point below 175*C, and (iii) reformer feed and other petroleum products having a final boiling point IM1OW150"C. The remits are reported to the nearest O* 1 percent by liquid volume, 2. OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 21 The sample is introduced into a gas chromatographic coIurnn containing a strongly polar liquid phase. The polar phase has ve:y. little affinity for saturated and olefinic hydrocarbons while exhib~tlng a pronounced selectivity for aromatics. This selectivity results in the eiution of all saturated and oIe6nic hydrocarbons in the products
described above prior to the conductivity or flame ionization ektion of benzene. 13it~er a thermal detector may be wed. Calibration is

performed by using synthetic blends of the aromatic compounds charged �~~ecification for
aviation gasoline (jint ratitin ).

6. CALIBRATION 6.1 Preparation of Standards - Prepare three standard blends indicated as blend 1, 2, and 3 in Table 2. To do this, pipette the exact volume ( in ml ) of each hydrocarbon indicated into a loo-ml flask. Fill to the 100-ml mark with one of the solvents listed in 4.5 and mix by inverting several times, 6.2 Select the instrument conditions and sample size so as to give necessary sensitivity and resolution. Xnject each standard blend into chromatograph at least twice, using the same volume of sample instrument conditions. If a sensitivity of less than maximum is needed measure the n-decane, iuternal standard and aromatic peaks, change attenuation so that the peaks are measured at not less than 25 percent full scale. the the and to the of

6.3 On blend 1 measure the height of the n-decane peak and the height of the valley between it and benzene. Express both on a common attenuation basis. Divide the height of the valley above the base line by the total height of the n-decane peak. This value shall not exceed O-5 for the column and conditions to be used. 6.4 Measure the area of all aromatic and internal of the following means: triangulation, planimeter, and-disc integrator, or electronic integrator. standard paper peak by any cut-out, ball-

NOTE-Because the C', and heavier compounds may not be completely resolved, peak height times one half the width or retention time shall not be used as a means,of measuring the area.

6.5 If a different attenuation was used for part of the chromatogram, correct to a constant attenuation basis by multiplying the areas where lower sensitivity was used by the ratio:

Fill to the lo-ml mark with sample and mix by inverting several times. 7.2 Using the exact instrument conditions as were used in the calibration, inject the same volume of sample containing the internal standard. Change the attenuation if necessary so as to measure the area of the internal standard and aromatic peaks with not less than 25 percent chart deflection on attenuated peaks. 8. 9. PRECISION

9.1 The criteria shown in Fig. 2 and 3 should be used for judging the acceptability of results ( 95 percent probability ). The precision statements are based on results from five laboratories analysing five samples and should be considered tentative, pending further work and statistical evaluation. Electronic integrators were used by all of the cooperating laboratories. Less precise results may be obtained if other methods of measurement are used.
9.1.1 Rejeatability -

amounts shown amount present,
